+"""Rarely used code, loaded on first use (off the package import path)."""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+
+from .base import merge, pop_top_pairs, render_token
+
+
+def save_vocab(self, vocab_file):
+    # the human-readable .vocab file of Tokenizer.save (lossy: errors='replace')
+    inverted_merges = {idx: pair for pair, idx in self.merges.items()}
+    with open(vocab_file, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        for idx, token in self.vocab.items():
+            s = render_token(token)
+            if idx in inverted_merges:
+                idx0, idx1 = inverted_merges[idx]
+                s0 = render_token(self.vocab[idx0])
+                s1 = render_token(self.vocab[idx1])
+                f.write(f"[{s0}][{s1}] -> [{s}] {idx}\n")
+            else:
+                f.write(f"[{s}] {idx}\n")
+
+
+def apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as base.apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list
+    over the positions plus a lazily validated heap of (rank, position); each
+    round merges the minimal rank's first pair left to right, like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+

+        p0 = ids[j]
+        p1 = ids[j+1]
+        last = len(ranks) - 1 # last pair position
+        newids = []
+        ext = newids.extend
+        app = newids.append
+        newranks = []
+        rext = newranks.extend
+        rapp = newranks.append
+        index = ranks.index
+        s = 0 # start of the not yet copied part of ids / ranks
+        first = True
+        while True:
+            k -= 1
+            if ids[j] == p0 and ids[j+1] == p1:
+                # merge the occurrence at j (same left-to-right order as merge())
+                if s < j:
+                    if not first:
+                        rapp(merges_get((idx, ids[s]), inf))
+                    rext(ranks[s:j-1])
+                    rapp(merges_get((ids[j-1], idx), inf))
+                    ext(ids[s:j])
+                elif not first:
+                    rapp(merges_get((idx, idx), inf))
+                app(idx)
+                first = False
+                s = j + 2
+                if j < last and ranks[j+1] == idx:
+                    k -= 1 # overlapping position j+1 is skipped
+                start = s
+            else:
+                start = j + 1
+            if not k:
+                break
+            j = index(idx, start)
+        if s <= last + 1:
+            rapp(merges_get((idx, ids[s]), inf))

+        ranks = newranks

+    # with a merge (as a pair token or as a minted token)
+    if not merges:

+    table = _replace_table(merges)
+    if table is None:
+        return None
+    for ps, c in table:
+        if "\xff" in ps or c == "\xff":
+            return None
+    return table
+
+
+def _split_specials(text, special):
+    # re.split of the escaped tokens alternation (non-empty tokens), no regex
+    parts = []
+    pos = 0
+    while True:
+        best = -1
+        for k in special:
+            i = text.find(k, pos)
+            if i != -1 and (best == -1 or i < best):

+        if best == -1:
+            parts.append(text[pos:])
+            return parts
+        parts += text[pos:best], tok
+        pos = best + len(tok)
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    # long sequences (loaded on first use), see _slow.apply_merges_heap
+    from ._slow import apply_merges_heap
+    return apply_merges_heap(ids, merges)

journal.text:
I tried to cut encode_ir by shrinking what encoding loads. My first idea was inside minbpe/regex.py. After that I moved code that encoding never runs out of minbpe/_heap.py and into the lazily loaded minbpe/_slow.py, behind thin stubs, with the bodies unchanged. That covered the long-sequence heap merger, the .vocab writer, and the body of replace_control_characters.

The regex.py-only attempt made things worse: encode_ir ratio 1.0299, rejected. Moving code out of _heap.py reached 0.9907, then 0.9901, both rejected against the required 0.9900. Trimming base.py further got 0.9876 (390509394 vs 395399999), accepted in my sandbox, with train_ir at 0.9996 and identical outputs. I submitted it at 200 changed lines and it is queued for replay.

I now think encode cost here is mostly fixed import and load work, and the margins are thin. The gain is barely past the bar and could vanish under replay noise.

Next I should look at the hot per-chunk encode loop itself instead of load size.
